title: Marienfeld Monastery - Teuto-Navigator
content: Founded in 1185, the Cistercian monastery of Marienfeld was one of the most important monasteries in Westphalia until its dissolution in 1803, and its spiritual influence was widely felt in the Westphalian region. An outstanding example of Cistercian architecture is the late Romanesque abbey church, whose architecture had a lasting influence on other important church buildings in the Westphalia region and the Baltic Sea area. Together with the baroque abbey building, which borders the church to the west, the old abbey church characterizes the old farmyard of the former monastery. To the east and west, this is dominated by the farm buildings built in the first half of the 18th century, making the entire monastery courtyard an oasis of peace and relaxation. In addition, the 1200-metre-long Cistercian Trail offers a historical tour around the monastery grounds. The 618-year-old history of the monastery is vividly explained on 13 steles. The monastery can be visited as part of a guided tour.

Hidden away in the hills of Austria, just outside the city of Vienna, is Heiligenkreuz Abbey. Dating back to 1133, it is the oldest continuous Cistercian abbey in the world. EWTN's Colm Flynn gets a rare look inside the abbey, where visitors are not normally permitted, and meets one of the monks who has dedicated their life to daily prayer and worship.
